messages.author: 127061c90ba8b71d
messages.subject: INLA Crash with ePower package
parts:
Hi all,

I am running Windows 10 and up-to-date versions of R and RStudio. I am working on a power analysis for a BACI experiment with the epower package. When I try to use the fitData( ) function to bring in an .xlsx file I get an error message that the INLA program (which is a package dependency) has crashed. I have scoured help boards and none of the solutions have worked for me. Part of the issue is that I don't know how to manipulate inla arguments through the functions of a different package. 

The code, which is quite short, is reproduced below and the input file is attached. FWIW, I have not had this problem when running the exact same code on macOS Big Sur (11.6). I am attempting to run the code on a windows desktop machine to avoid having the long run time of the code on my personal laptop.

Thank you for any thoughts.


##### BACI Power Analysis #####

rm(list=ls())

.libPaths("C:/Program Files/R/R-4.2.2rc/library") #set library path for install packages

#install three packages that are dependencies for epower
install.packages("doParallel")
install.packages("XLConnect")
install.packages("INLA", repos=c(getOption("repos"), INLA="https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable"), dep=TRUE)

library(doParallel)
library(XLConnect)
library(INLA)

#download epower package from .tar.gz file (link below) and install using Install Packages (under Tools) in RStudio

#https://github.com/bmtglobal/epower/blob/master/epower_1.3.tar.gz
library(epower)

#run analysis
fitData() #brings in .xlsx data ---> INLA CRASH HAPPENING AT THIS STEP

assessPower() #runs power analysis


######## end of code ##########

Hi,

First thing that comes to mind is potential memory issues on windows. How much memory do you have on the windows machine compared with the Mac? It seems the best use of windows with inla is to run it under WSL (i.e. the windows linux system; a bit of a paradox…).

Finn
